candidates.text: Urban green spaces have become a key part of conversations about public health and city planning in recent years. Parks give residents room to exercise, unwind, and spend time with others. They also provide shade in warm weather and habitats for birds and insects. Yet a park’s value depends on more than its size. Its accessibility and upkeep, along with the needs of nearby residents, affect how often people use it. A large park that is hard to reach may be less useful than a smaller park within walking distance. City planners should weigh the total amount of green space alongside the everyday experience of those who visit. Investment in parks should include regular maintenance, clear paths, and ways for the community to offer feedback.

candidates.text: Urban green spaces have become a key part of conversations about public health and city planning in recent years. Parks give residents somewhere to exercise, unwind, and spend time with others. They can provide shade in warm weather and serve as habitats for birds and insects, too. Yet a park’s value depends on more than its size. How easy it is to reach, how well it is maintained, and what nearby residents need all affect how often people use it. A sprawling park that is hard to get to may be less useful than a smaller space within walking distance. City planners should weigh the total amount of green space alongside the experience of the people who use it. Park investment should include regular upkeep, well-defined paths, and ways for the community to share feedback.
